text.p: Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc rose Tuesday to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said most ADRs were following the rest of the New York markets higher.

The Dow industrials fell almost 200 points on Monday after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto suggested Tokyo might sell U.S. government securities. Finance Ministry officials later said the remarks had been misconstrued.
Traders said ADRs were characterized by bargain-hunting. One said of Monday's drop, "You sell it (a stock) at the opening and you buy it back in the afternoon."
National Westminster was up 4-3/4 to a 12-month high of 82-1/4 after the Financial Times newspaper reported the bank was "definitely in play."
Among other European ADRs, Dutch software company Baan Co NV was up 1-3/8 to 68, above its 12-month high.
ADRs in Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd's initial public offering were at 10-7/8 after opening at 11-1/2.
Pilipino Telephone Co was unchanged at 62-1/2 after the Philippines' APC Group said it was buying shares in the mobile phone company. APC denied it was making a takeover bid.
Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose 2-5/16 to 147-1/16.
Advancers led decliners 273 to 185 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.38 percent in late morning and volume was 26 million ADRS.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
